messages:
sre-oncall: APAC GPU pool degraded, autoscaler firing but new nodes failing healthchecks. Started DNS-based traffic shift to eu-west and lowered TTL to 30s ~1950001234. Seeing partial traffic still going to APAC edge. Anyone seeing resolver caches holding the old records?

maya: same, ~40% of requests to apac edge returning 504 timeout. Quick dig from my laptop: 
```
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 service.redwood-inference.internal A
203.0.113.45   # APAC LB
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 service.redwood-inference.internal A
198.51.100.12  # EU LB
```

alex: we do have split-horizon for some enterprise customers (internal resolvers pointed at our on-prem NS). Those resolvers can have stale negative/positive caches. Did we update the edge-steer config for the lb-ip? run: 
```
curl -sS https://ops-api/edge/steer/dump | jq '.rules | length'
```

netops: confirmed: route withdraw for apac LB ip wasn't executed because the anycast announcement is still present in our fabric. We can withdraw the specific /32 for lb-ip-203.0.113.45 from apac ASNs in ~2m.

deploy-bot: DNS record change (TTL=30) pushed to Route53 at 1950001265, change-id: C1234567890. Most public resolvers updated within 60s.

khalid: lowering TTL to 10s would speed propagation but increases query rate and costs. propose TTL=15s for 20 minutes while we complete withdraw. thoughts?

maya: corporate proxies are the pain here. Some of our largest customers have internal resolvers that mirror old A records; even after route withdrawal they keep returning the APAC IP until cache expiry. We should 1) withdraw route, 2) set very low TTL, 3) where possible, push 302->eu from apac edge for Host: header match.

sre-oncall: Plan: 
1) netops withdraw apac LB /32 now.
2) set TTL=15s for 20m in Route53 and Cloud DNS.
3) run a dig sweep from public probes + our corp customer probes and post results here.
4) if any corp resolver still returns apac ip after withdraw, open customer cache flush ticket.
Commands: 
```
# route withdraw (netops)
ssh netops@bgp-router "sudo zebractl withdraw 203.0.113.45/32"
# route53 change (dns)
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZ --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"service.redwood-inference.internal","Type":"A","TTL":15,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"198.51.100.12"}]}}]}'
```

netops: Withdrawing now — BGP withdraw issued to apac peers. Will confirm next-hop state.

alex: dig sweep after withdraw (public probes + corp probe): 
```
# from probe-1 (us-east): 198.51.100.12
# from probe-2 (eu-west): 198.51.100.12
# from corp-proxy-ny (customer X): 203.0.113.45  <-- still APAC
```
Mapping shows ~95% traffic now to EU, but corp-proxy-ny and corp-proxy-sf still return APAC IP. I'm opening ticket with Customer X to request resolver cache flush; adding contact.

khalid: agree to keep TTL=15s for 20m. we'll monitor QPS on authoritative ns and cost impact. If query surge > threshold revert to 30s.

maya: pushed temporary edge rule: any request that hits APAC edge with header "X-Geo: apac" gets 302 to eu endpoint while we force resolver fixes. That reduces error surface for users behind stubborn resolvers.

sre-oncall: monitoring: 5xx rate back to baseline after 7m. autoscaler paused for new node adds to avoid creating unhealthy nodes; will re-enable once traffic stable. Post-incident next steps: record split-horizon resolver checklist and prefer route-withdraw-first for future region shifts.

deploy-bot: change C1234567890 status -> INSYNC at 1950001800.

alex: still seeing a couple of corporate resolvers after 12m; sent customer cache-flush request and provided diagnostics: dig output + tracepath.

sre-oncall: Incident stabilized. Will roll TTL back to 300s in 1h if no regressions. Filing incident doc: https://internal.redwood/incidents/1950001234. Adding postmortem owner: maya. :white_check_mark:

netops: noted: need automated check that anycast withdraws are tied to DNS failover steps to avoid this partial-propagation mismatch.

maya: adding action item to postmortem: update runbook to include probing corporate resolver list + customer comms template.

sre-oncall: closing thread for now, will update appendix once TTL rollback done. Thanks all for quick turn.
